x: The Cross Country Captain would like to see more of Len Herbert, Archie Bedford and Peter Hitchcock, to mention a few. Jack Goswell is waiting to see young Joe Scamell, Gordon Waddingham, Percy Wilson, and a contributor who calls himself "Spotter" adds his observations on what he "sees and hears" -

Peter Hitchcock had the joy of running over the newly laid stretch of road round Gatwick Airport and although losing ground on the leading clubs he managed to pull us back to 7th with a steady performance which should add to his experience for next year.
Len Bishop and Eddie Short should have been at least ten places higher than their 42nd and 43rd, and Peter Hitchcock should also have been better positioned than 52nd.

Pete Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Len Bishop were next, in the 170's while the rest of our men were back in the 200's. The next view of the field was soon after the first lap had ended, and Walker had moved up to Gebbett and Short and Moore had also progressed about fifteen places and were running well.
39, P.Newell 77, C.W.Walker 134, E.Gebbett 175, C.Shippen 200, P.Hitchcock 264, D.Baulch 288, J.Dooley 307, E.Short 319, L.C.Bishop

In John Moore, Ken Jones and Robin Weate we have a acquired runners of high quality and Club Spirit and the improvement of George Flanagan, Peter Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Bob Glover promises well for the future.

Pete Hitchcock, Clive Shippen and Len Bishop were next, in the 170’s … At the conclusion of the next lap Walker had left Gebbett and was now 44th but was having great difficulty in making any further progress …
